title: Constrained-output telemetry & automated repair scenario suite
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Purpose: build a focused scenario suite and telemetry harness that exercises constrained-decoding failure modes (truncated JSON, sentinel loss, partial stream insertion, interleaved tool calls) and validates both detection and automated repair heuristics. Scope includes: synthetic corpora for adversarial schema breaks, token-level sentinel insertion tests, latency/cost measurement for repair flows, and an observable signal surface (metrics, traces, example replays) so Console and Optimize teams can reason about regressions. Goals: (1) surface realistic failure signals with stable thresholds, (2) exercise repair strategies (schema-aware reemit, prefix fallback, fallback model variants), and (3) produce reproducible tickets/PRs with minimal flakiness for CI and canary runs.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic harness can inject the following failure classes against the constrained decoder: truncated payload, corrupted sentinel, interleaved toolcall noise, and token-drop; each class is configurable by seed and intensity.
For each failure class, the harness emits metrics: detection latency (ms), token overhead caused by repair, success rate of repair within 3 attempts, and downstream schema-validated pass rate.
At least 5 automated repair policies are implemented and testable: schema-heal-reemit, greedy-sentinel-repair, prefix-fallback-to-short-schema, backoff-with-variant-model, and no-repair (control).
Console dashboards (per-test and aggregate) show trends for detection latency and repair regressions; example traces can be linked to PRs.
Suite runs in CI (non-blocking smoke) and as a nightly regression harness producing artifacts for triage (replay inputs, model outputs, repaired outputs).
False-positive repair triggers are under 2% on a held-out benign corpus.
Documentation: design doc, runbook for investigating failures, and a short guide for PM/Design to interpret signals are published.
Updated APIs or decoder flags required for testability are landed behind feature flags and documented in the PR.
Updated_at is after created_at and due_date is realistic.
tasks: Design adversarial input generator (schema-aware and schema-agnostic modes).
Define telemetry schema: metrics, labels, and span annotations for trace correlation.
Implement harness that can drive the constrained decoder with deterministic seeds and inject failure classes.
Implement 5 repair policies as testable modules behind feature flags.
Integrate harness with CI and nightly job runner; add artifact upload (replays + examples).
Add Console dashboard widgets (telemetry team collaboration).
Author playbook/runbook describing triage steps and recommended immediate mitigations.
test_plan: Unit tests: small deterministic seeds for each failure class; assert repair module invoked and output matches schema.
Property tests: run 10k randomized inputs (fast mode) and assert detection latency histogram is stable across runs.
Fuzzing: adversarial templates with variable token corruption rates; ensure at least one repair policy recovers the schema in >50% cases at medium intensity.
Canary: run suite on 5% of production-like traffic via mirror; compare repair policy token overhead and latencies against control.
Nightly regression: full corpus run producing artifacts and automatic regression detection guards (statistical thresholds).
Manual validation: PM/Design review of representative repaired outputs and false-positive cases.
notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive repair (reemit/wider beam) improves pass-rate but increases token cost and latency; we will capture both metrics so Optimize can weigh trade-offs.
We will keep repair policies modular so downstream routing/Optimize can pick default per-customer SLA tier.
Telemetry schema proposal: metric names prefixed with redwood.decoder.repair.*, labels: failure_class, repair_policy, model_variant, canary_bucket.

Related artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Constrained+Output+Telemetry+Design , initial generator proto: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C4 , decoder flag PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2407 .
Collaboration: Console (dashboards) owner is Jonas Meyer, Optimize owner is Mei-Ling Chen, QA lead is Ruben Ortiz.
We intentionally avoid changing public API contracts; any required hooks will be behind feature flags and documented in runtime-1.24 release notes.
